players.product: dimensional & materials metrology for leading-edge nodes

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 revenue reached $222.6 million, above the guidance midpoint of $220 million and up 14% year-over-year. Product revenue was approximately 75% logic and foundry / 25% memory, and 3 customers and 4 territories each contributed 10% or more of product revenue. Gross margin was 57.6% GAAP / 59.6% non-GAAP, in the upper end of the 57% to 60% target model, attributed to a favorable product mix. Operating expenses rose to $67.5 million GAAP / $62 million non-GAAP as R&D and sales and marketing spending ramped in a targeted manner; operating margin was 27% GAAP / 32% non-GAAP. The GAAP effective tax rate of approximately 11% reflected the release of uncertain tax positions after a tax assessment audit (approximately 16% non-GAAP). EPS was $1.94 GAAP and $2.14 non-GAAP, above the $2.11 guidance midpoint.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenue $222.6 million, up 14% year-over-year; non-GAAP gross margin 59.6%, operating margin 32%, EPS $2.14; product mix approximately 75% logic and foundry / 25% memory

quarterly_data.signal: FULL-YEAR 2025 was a record: revenue of $880.6 million, up 31% year-over-year, with record GAAP and non-GAAP profitability and EPS growing 29% year-over-year. Gross margin was 57.4% GAAP / 59% non-GAAP; operating margin 29% GAAP / 33% non-GAAP, in the upper end of the 28% to 33% target model; EPS $7.96 GAAP / $8.62 non-GAAP. Geographic split: China 33%, Taiwan 29%, Korea 16%, U.S. 9%, other territories 13%. Nova ended 2025 with more than $1.6 billion in cash, cash equivalents, bank deposits and marketable securities, generated $218 million of free cash flow in 2025, and invests more than 15% of revenues in R&D. SERVICES delivered record quarterly and annual revenue, driven by capacity installation, adoption of value-added yield-improvement services and a shift from Time and Materials towards annual service contracts.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 revenue $880.6 million, up 31% year-over-year; non-GAAP operating margin 33%; non-GAAP EPS $8.62; free cash flow $218 million; China 33%, Taiwan 29%, Korea 16%, U.S. 9%

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 guidance: revenue between $222 million and $232 million, GAAP EPS $1.90 to $2.02 and non-GAAP EPS $2.13 to $2.25. At the midpoint: gross margin approximately 56% GAAP / approximately 58% non-GAAP; operating expenses decreasing to approximately $65 million GAAP / approximately $60 million non-GAAP; non-GAAP financial income approximately $16 million; effective tax rate approximately 16%. CFO Guy Kizner said the 58% gross-margin guide (plus/minus 1% point, versus 59.6% reported in Q4) reflects the specific product mix of the quarter - 'nothing really changed structurally' - and that margins should be judged on an annual basis. CEO Gaby Waisman said Nova sees no correlation between memory pricing and its gross margin.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 2026 revenue between $222 million and $232 million; non-GAAP EPS $2.13 to $2.25; non-GAAP gross margin approximately 58%

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 OUTLOOK: management anticipates WFE growth 'in the low double digits' in 2026 and aims to outperform it, but said it is still early in the year to indicate any specific number for the outperformance. Current order patterns point to ANOTHER GROWTH YEAR for Nova, with momentum expected to build through the first half and ACCELERATE IN THE SECOND HALF; management also sees the first half of 2026 higher than 2025. Named growth drivers: (1) advanced logic - proliferation of gate-all-around across all leading manufacturers with increasing process-control intensity; (2) a healthy recovery in DRAM and continued build-out of HBM capacity; (3) a growing contribution from hybrid bonding in advanced packaging. Rising design complexity and new integration methods such as backside power delivery and hybrid bonding are broadening the need for precise metrology, and some manufacturers have already announced higher CapEx plans, which management called very encouraging while noting it takes time for those to turn into orders and revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: WFE in the low double digits in 2026; another growth year for Nova with momentum accelerating in the second half

quarterly_data.signal: GATE-ALL-AROUND: in Q4 a global leading logic customer (not named on the call) selected Nova's INTEGRATED METROLOGY portfolio for CMP applications across gate-all-around processes - after a comprehensive evaluation it adopted Nova's FULL CMP PRODUCT SUITE, extending an earlier back-end deployment into front-end high-volume manufacturing; multiple orders have already been placed for 2026, with more expected as capacity ramps. Nova describes itself as a foundational partner in the industry's transition to next-generation architectures, 'well positioned across all 4 players' in gate-all-around, and on track for its $500 million cumulative gate-all-around revenue target for '24 to '26, with 2026 expected higher than 2025. At 3-nanometer the metrology intensity is not as high as at gate-all-around 2-nanometer, 'but it's still very significant', so any advanced-node investment benefits Nova. R&D is developing a new metrology solution that combines Nova's optical and materials metrology with physical and AI-driven modeling, aimed at gate-all-around, CFET and advanced memory.
quarterly_data.figure: $500 million cumulative gate-all-around revenue for '24 to '26 on track; multiple 2026 orders from a leading logic customer for the full CMP integrated-metrology suite

quarterly_data.signal: ADVANCED PACKAGING revenue rose more than 60% year-over-year in 2025 to approximately 20% of product revenue, with traction across both dimensional and chemical metrology platforms and broad adoption of Nova's dedicated products; the Nova WMC optical metrology system gained traction in advanced packaging and high-bandwidth memory. Of that 20%, about 1/4 to 1/3 (depending on the quarter) is HIGH-BANDWIDTH MEMORY and the rest is logic. For 2026 management expects double-digit ('strong double-digit') growth in advanced packaging and a growing contribution from HYBRID BONDING; management said advanced packaging is relatively new for Nova, with more and more of its products penetrating and gaining share there. Nova says it is engaged with all players, has sufficient manufacturing capacity including clean-room capacity for advanced packaging in particular, and sees share-gain traction with its stand-alone OCD solutions for packaging and advanced packaging.
quarterly_data.figure: advanced packaging revenue up more than 60% in 2025 to approximately 20% of product revenue; about 1/4 to 1/3 of it high-bandwidth memory; double-digit growth expected in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: SHARE GAINS AND LAB-TO-FAB PRODUCTS: per Gartner's latest report for 2024, Nova became SECOND in market share in CD and film metrology with about 25% share, and management sees continued share gains across the portfolio. The ELIPSON materials metrology solution was selected as TOOL OF RECORD by a leading foundry (not named) for advanced gate-all-around production, with additional tools 'at another leading logic and memory customers', plus repeat orders and proliferation from R&D into high-volume manufacturing. METRION was recently qualified at a gate-all-around logic customer and a leading memory manufacturer (adopted for gate-all-around and for advanced 3D NAND and DRAM manufacturing) - both at an early phase of proliferation, with the goal of MULTIPLE TOOLS PER FAB, as XPS scaled historically. Nova has just shipped its 300TH XPS TOOL. Share gains are also coming in front-end copper dual damascene for the chemical metrology portfolio.
quarterly_data.figure: 300th XPS tool shipped; second in CD and film metrology market share at about 25% (Gartner report for 2024)

quarterly_data.signal: MEMORY: memory was 25% of Q4 product revenue, and 2025 memory results were a record, driven primarily by DRAM, where manufacturers expanded adoption of Nova's materials and chemical metrology offering. For 2026 management sees a healthy DRAM recovery and continued build-out of HBM capacity, and names leading-edge advanced logic and DRAM (plus advanced packaging) as the main growth vectors. On NAND, 'we do see some signs of improvement', but Nova is still waiting for an inflection point similar to the one seen in DRAM and HBM.
quarterly_data.figure: memory 25% of Q4 product revenue; 2025 memory a record, led by DRAM; NAND inflection not yet seen

quarterly_data.signal: CHINA was 39% of Nova's business in 2024 and normalized to about 33% in 2025; management expects it to continue at AROUND 30% of sales. External data shows process control in China went down, but Nova's China business went up nominally. China has shorter lead times, which reduced visibility, but current trends give management confidence in steady Chinese investment and at least the nominal level of business in 2026. Because China focuses on mature nodes while advanced-node and DRAM investment grows, China's share of Nova's sales is expected to go down even if nominal sales stay flat.
quarterly_data.figure: China 39% of business in 2024, about 33% in 2025, expected around 30% of sales

quarterly_data.signal: CAPACITY AND LEAD TIMES: Nova made significant investments over the last year to expand manufacturing capacity and says it has enough to support its growth outlook, including clean-room capacity for advanced packaging. In 2026 it is building NEW PRODUCTION CAPACITY IN ASIA (for cost efficiency and to sit closer to key customers and supply-chain partners) and launching a new ERP system to manage growing volume. Management agreed there is MORE PRESSURE ON LEAD TIMES, which also affects visibility; it said the pressure comes from customers needing to turn CapEx into WFE and actual deliveries into the fab, and applies across the materials, chemical and dimensional metrology portfolios. Asked whether the optical-component constraints cited by peers are a driver, management said no. Nova is working with its suppliers and supply chain to secure both materials and capacity for the anticipated 2026 growth.

SILICON PHOTONICS was named as an emerging segment fueled by the AI era: it requires very high-accuracy measurements of optical structures such as waveguides and modulators, with precise alignment and 3D characterization, which management said 'opens new opportunities for Nova'.
